clue.text: Soldier dies after dropping ecstasy in Heaven

parts.note: a PARA is a paratrooper, a common crossword soldier

indicators.note: the letter for ecstasy drops lower in the word dies, which in a down clue means further down the light

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A soldier's death after giving up a party drug is pictured as reaching Heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after dropping' moves the E of 'dies' down to the end of that word; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a synonym for Heaven, the abode of the blessed.

clue.text: Corporation has invested large surplus

indicators.note: to invest is to put money into, so the belly here takes the large letter inside it

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, a gut
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A company has put a big surplus of money into investments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a company, but it is the old slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut is an excessive supply, which is a surplus.

clue.text: Gangs said to go round looking for sex

indicators.note: said signals that the word for gangs is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: crews are gangs of workers or sailors

explanation.surface: Gangs are reported to roam about in search of sexual partners.
explanation.definitionFit: To cruise is slang for touring a place in search of a sexual partner.

clue.text: Free lunch lacking core ingredient turned out to be pleasant

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are tipped out and rearranged into a fresh order
the central ingredient of the word lunch, its middle letter, is missing

explanation.surface: A free lunch missing its main ingredient still proved enjoyable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking core ingredient' removes N, the middle letter of LUNCH; 'turned out' rearranges FREE plus LUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerful describes something bright and agreeable, close to pleasant.

clue.text: What reveals and, in a manner of speaking, inspires?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the manner of speaking draws the letter a inside it

parts.note: diction is one's manner of speaking or enunciation

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what reveals things and, figuratively, inspires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' reads as 'figuratively', but splits into IN, A and a word for speech; 'inspires' (breathes in) puts the A inside, giving DICATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An indication is a sign that shows or reveals something.

clue.text: Play with retracting pencil or felt-tip pens

indicators.note: a retracting pen point is drawn back, so the enclosed letters read in the opposite direction
to pen is to enclose, so these words hold the answer's letters within them

explanation.surface: Someone toys with a retractable pencil or with felt-tip pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' hides CILORF in 'pencil or felt-tip'; 'retracting' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic is to play about merrily.

clue.text: Close-fitting leotard I modelled

indicators.note: modelled suggests the letters are shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: A dancer showing off a snug leotard she wore on the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelled' rearranges LEOTARD I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailored clothes are cut to fit the body closely.

clue.text: Half believed police department's tapped judge

indicators.note: tapped as in a phone or a cask tapped into, with the department going inside
only the first half of the word for believed is kept

parts.note: to have deemed is to have believed or judged
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Police wiretaps a half-trusted suspect before a judge rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' keeps the first half of DEEMED, and ''s tapped' puts the department inside it; CID is Britain's plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a matter is to settle it, which is to decide it.

clue.text: American expelled from country for going without fare

indicators.note: the American is thrown out of the country, so that letter leaves it

parts.note: Hungary is a country in central Europe

explanation.surface: An American deported from a country for not paying his fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like a ticket price but means food.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone going without food is hungry.

clue.text: Player worries when start of test is delayed

indicators.note: delayed means coming later, so that letter moves further along the word

parts.note: something that eats you worries you

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A cricketer frets when the start of a Test match is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is delayed' moves the T of EATS later. East is one of the four players at bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four seats are North, South, East and West, so East is a player.

clue.text: Unpalatable cases initially cause revulsion beyond belief

indicators.note: to case is to encase, so the unpalatable word wraps around the letters

parts.note: unpalatable food is inedible

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the next words are taken

explanation.surface: Revolting food in some instances causes disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes C and R from 'cause revulsion'; 'cases' puts them inside INEDIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Incredible means impossible to believe.

clue.text: Taste is pretty much wasted on writer

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after the writer

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen, standing for the writer

indicators.note: pretty much means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to have blown money is to have wasted it, blew

explanation.surface: Good taste is supposedly lost on an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' is past tense here, as money is blown; 'pretty much' drops its last letter, and 'on' in an across clue places it after the writer's nib.
explanation.definitionFit: A nibble is a small bite, a taste of food.

clue.text: Official pitch inexperienced reporter typed up about waste

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reversed letters surround the waste
in a down clue up means the words are written from the bottom, read backwards

parts.note: tar is a black pitch
a cub is a novice journalist
urea is a waste product found in urine

explanation.surface: An official describes a novice journalist's typed pitch as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'typed up' reverses TARCUB to BUCRAT, and 'about' puts it round UREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureaucrat is an official in a government department.

clue.text: Man pledged backing from French Resistance

indicators.note: backing means supporting from behind, so the man comes after

parts.note: de is French for from
a fiancé is a man pledged to be married

explanation.surface: A man promised help to the French Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' puts FIANCE behind DE. Resistance appears capitalised to suggest the wartime French movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance to authority.

clue.text: Improve state of disturbed heartless children

indicators.note: disturbed suggests letters thrown into disorder
heartless means the central letters of children are removed

explanation.surface: Improving the condition of troubled, callous children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes LD from CHILDREN; 'disturbed' rearranges CHIREN.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich something is to make it better in quality.

clue.text: What may have part to play in temperature falling in cold office?

definitions.text: What may have part to play

indicators.note: falling in a down clue means moving lower down the word

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
the offices is an old British euphemism for the lavatory, so a latrine

explanation.surface: A query about what has a role in temperatures dropping in a cold workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' is the British euphemism for a lavatory. 'falling in' moves the T of CLATRINE down to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is an instrument with its own orchestral part to play.

clue.text: This fish looks and sounds flat?

indicators.note: sounds says the word for flat is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a flat is a home, a place

explanation.surface: A fish that seems flat in look and dull in sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks and' adds that the plaice is a flatfish, so it looks flat as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a European flatfish.

clue.text: Managed to get reference suspect lied about

indicators.note: about means round, so the rearranged letters go round the reference
suspect suggests the letters are dubious and rearranged

parts.note: to cite is to refer to a source

explanation.surface: Someone extracted a citation the suspect had lied about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges 'lied' into ELID, and 'about' wraps it round the reference.
explanation.definitionFit: To have elicited something is to have succeeded in drawing it out.

clue.text: Religious teaching is unable to deny earlier beliefs

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject in Britain
is unable means can't

explanation.surface: A religion's teaching cannot disown its earlier creeds.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a former opinion publicly.

clue.text: Increase scope of criminal case and others under review

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of shape
review read as re-view, looking back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: et al is the Latin abbreviation for and others

explanation.surface: Widening a criminal case to bring others under scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges CASE into ESCA, and 'under review' reverses ETAL to LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate a matter is to widen its extent or intensity.

clue.text: Comparatively unbalanced means of presenting items for consumption

definitions.text: means of presenting items for consumption
definitions.meaning: a ... holds pieces of food such as kebab

explanation.definitionFit: Skew means slanted, and a skewer is a spit for serving food.

clue.text: Messenger from wedding cycled round front of church

indicators.note: round means the cycled letters surround the church letter
cycled means the end letter is moved round to the other end of the word

parts.note: a wedding is a union

indicators.note: front of gives only the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A messenger comes from a wedding having cycled round a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycled' moves the final N of UNION to the front, giving NUNIO, and 'round' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal ambassador, an envoy carrying the Pope's messages.

clue.text: Wanted joint passed to the audience

indicators.note: to the audience means heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: the knee is a joint; passed on means died, dead

explanation.surface: Someone wanted a cannabis joint passed round the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like the drug but means the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed means required, synonymous with wanted.

clue.text: Ordered cadet that is controlling tank to turn off

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters are put into a new order
controlling means holding, so these letters contain the tank

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
a vat is a large tank

explanation.surface: A cadet in a tank is ordered to switch something off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' rearranges 'cadet' into DEACT; 'controlling' means the IE of 'that is' holds the tank.
explanation.definitionFit: To deactivate is to stop something operating, switch it off.

clue.text: Send out introduction to elite university

indicators.note: introduction to means only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Sending out an introduction to a top university.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or discharge.

clue.text: Freelancer has vigour and style

indicators.note: has means holds, so the word freelancer contains the answer

explanation.surface: A self-employed worker shows energy and panache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' hides the letters in 'Freelancer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: élan, borrowed from French, is dash and flair carried off with energy, so it covers both vigour and style.

clue.text: Reverse management's reshuffle after married man is dismissed

indicators.note: a reshuffle reorders posts, so here the letters are reorganised
dismissed means removed, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: the word management, with its possessive ending acting only as a link to reshuffle
taken as written

explanation.surface: Management overturns a cabinet reshuffle after a married man is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is dismissed' takes MAN and M out of MANAGEMENT; 'reshuffle' rearranges AGEENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to nullify or reverse something.

clue.text: Support Harry meeting the Queen in person

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
to harry someone is to nag them
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Backing Prince Harry meeting the Queen face to face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person between thirteen and nineteen.
